events.title: Rider Advocate brief: 6 claims (0 void)
events.body:
C1: The $6.61 cancellation fee was levied on the rider, but the fee only arises in the two published situations and Ryde's own rule for a 'rider cancels' case is that any cancellation within 3 minutes of matching is not chargeable; here the rider cancelled at 18:25:30, only 2 min 30 s after acceptance at 18:23:00, i.e. inside the free window. [F2 F5] [NS-0 NS-4]
C2: There is no basis to treat the rider as a no-show (the only other route to the $6.61 fee): the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null) and the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so NS-1(i) and (ii) both fail. [F3 F4] [NS-0 NS-1 NS-2]
C3: GPS confirms the driver was never at the pickup point: his closest approach was 1806 m at 18:25:30 and he never came within 200 m, so the rider's statement that the driver was nowhere near is corroborated by the system record, not merely asserted. [F1 F2] [NS-1 NS-2]
C4: The rider's cancellation was prompt and in good faith: she asked for an ETA at 18:23 and the driver only answered 'About 5 min, traffic' at 18:24, so at the moment she cancelled the driver was still several minutes and over 1.8 km away — no rule requires her to keep waiting, and the $6.61 deduction is unexplained by any published additional charge. [F7 F8 F1 F5] [NS-4 FARE-1]
C5: Because the fee fail-conditions are made out, the full $6.61 charged should be returned to the rider as a Ryde voucher; the amount equals the cancellation fee actually charged (F5) and the disputed fee is to be waived in full rather than cash-refunded. [F5] [NS-2 NS-7]
C6: Separately from the outcome of this case, the driver's record shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days against only 777 trips plus 2 disputes flagged, which warrants sending his account for Ryde review as an additional account action. [F14] [NS-3 NS-7]
Weaknesses: The rider cancelled unilaterally rather than waiting for the driver, so the other side will argue she deprived the driver of the trip; F2 shows she cancelled at 18:25:30 and the driver's statement (F9) says 'I was on my way when the rider cancelled.' The counter is that NS-4 makes the 3-minute rule mechanical, and F1 shows the driver was still 1806 m away. | The rider does not get a free cancellation merely because the driver was late or far: NS-4 expressly says the driver not having arrived is not a ground for a free rider cancellation, and there is no ETA-based waiver rule to rely on (no ETA field in the case file). The case therefore rests on the 3-minute window in F2, not on the driver's lateness. | Traffic was mildly slow on Boon Lay Way (F10, speed band 3, 20-29 km/h) and the driver cited traffic in chat (F8); the driver may use this to argue he was reasonably en route, though F11 records no incident and F10 is a single 20-29 km/h band that cannot justify the 1806 m gap in F1. | The rider's own message (F7) shows she was still awaiting the driver rather than fleeing a no-show, and a judge could read the 2 min 30 s cancellation as opportunistic; the answer is that NS-4 sets no motive test — any cancellation within 3:00 is free. | The requested remedy is a voucher, not cash (NS-7), so the client does not recover money in hand even if the claim succeeds.

claims.assertion: The $6.61 cancellation fee was levied on the rider, but the fee only arises in the two published situations and Ryde's own rule for a 'rider cancels' case is that any cancellation within 3 minutes of matching is not chargeable; here the rider cancelled at 18:25:30, only 2 min 30 s after acceptance at 18:23:00, i.e. inside the free window.

There is no basis to treat the rider as a no-show (the only other route to the $6.61 fee): the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null) and the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so NS-1(i) and (ii) both fail.

GPS confirms the driver was never at the pickup point: his closest approach was 1806 m at 18:25:30 and he never came within 200 m, so the rider's statement that the driver was nowhere near is corroborated by the system record, not merely asserted.

The rider's cancellation was prompt and in good faith: she asked for an ETA at 18:23 and the driver only answered 'About 5 min, traffic' at 18:24, so at the moment she cancelled the driver was still several minutes and over 1.8 km away — no rule requires her to keep waiting, and the $6.61 deduction is unexplained by any published additional charge.

Because the fee fail-conditions are made out, the full $6.61 charged should be returned to the rider as a Ryde voucher; the amount equals the cancellation fee actually charged (F5) and the disputed fee is to be waived in full rather than cash-refunded.

Separately from the outcome of this case, the driver's record shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days against only 777 trips plus 2 disputes flagged, which warrants sending his account for Ryde review as an additional account action.

weaknesses: The rider cancelled unilaterally rather than waiting for the driver, so the other side will argue she deprived the driver of the trip; F2 shows she cancelled at 18:25:30 and the driver's statement (F9) says 'I was on my way when the rider cancelled.' The counter is that NS-4 makes the 3-minute rule mechanical, and F1 shows the driver was still 1806 m away.

The rider does not get a free cancellation merely because the driver was late or far: NS-4 expressly says the driver not having arrived is not a ground for a free rider cancellation, and there is no ETA-based waiver rule to rely on (no ETA field in the case file). The case therefore rests on the 3-minute window in F2, not on the driver's lateness.

Traffic was mildly slow on Boon Lay Way (F10, speed band 3, 20-29 km/h) and the driver cited traffic in chat (F8); the driver may use this to argue he was reasonably en route, though F11 records no incident and F10 is a single 20-29 km/h band that cannot justify the 1806 m gap in F1.

The rider's own message (F7) shows she was still awaiting the driver rather than fleeing a no-show, and a judge could read the 2 min 30 s cancellation as opportunistic; the answer is that NS-4 sets no motive test — any cancellation within 3:00 is free.
The requested remedy is a voucher, not cash (NS-7), so the client does not recover money in hand even if the claim succeeds.

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.95)
events.body:
The rider cancelled the trip herself (cancelled_by = rider) 2 min 30 s after acceptance, i.e. 150 s inside the 3-minute free window [F2], so the only fee route open under the cancellation policy is the rider-cancellation branch invoked through NS-0, and that branch charges nothing for a cancellation made within 3 minutes of matching [F2][NS-0][NS-4]. The $6.61 on record [F2][F5] therefore has no billing basis.

The alternative route to the same $6.61 — treating the rider as a no-show — also fails. The platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at null) [F3] and the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at null) [F4], so NS-1 conditions (i) and (ii) cannot be satisfied and the fee must be refunded in full under NS-2 [F3][F4][NS-1][NS-2]. The GPS record independently confirms the rider's account: the driver's closest approach was 1806 m at the moment of cancellation and he never came within 200 m [F1][F2], so the system record, which prevails over statements, corroborates the complaint rather than the driver's "I was on my way" chat and statement [F1][F2][F4][NS-1].

The driver's traffic explanation does not create a fee entitlement, and it does not need to be resolved: one mid-band reading of 20–29 km/h on Boon Lay Way with no incidents recorded and fair weather [F10][F11][F12] neither satisfies RD-4 (which concerns route deviation, not cancellation fees) nor defeats the mechanical 3-minute rule in NS-4 [F10][F11][F12][NS-4]. His chat ETA of "About 5 min" [F8] is contradicted by the 1806 m system record [F1], but the outcome rests on the 3-minute window alone.

Amount: the disputed item is the cancellation fee actually charged, $6.61 [F2][F5]; no other published add-on (waiting fee, ERP, platform fee) is disputed and surge was 1.0× [F5][F6][FARE-1]. Refund is the full $6.61, payable as a Ryde voucher and not in cash [F5][NS-7][NS-2].

Account action: the case does not establish a driver violation — no "I'm Here" tap was made and no arrival was asserted [F3][F4], so the RD-6/NS-2 flag_account preconditions (upheld violation in this case, or abuse of the arrival/waiting button) are not met; the driver's 2 prior upheld no-show disputes [F14] are profile data and cannot alone trigger an account action here [F14][NS-1][NS-2].

ruling.recommended_action: Reverse the $6.61 cancellation fee and issue the rider a Ryde voucher worth $6.61 (NS-7); no account action against the driver from this case.

certificate: ✗ NS-4 rider cancelled more than 3 min after matching [case] 150 s after acceptance (F2)
allowed outcomes: refund_full; amount = cancellation fee $6.61

claims.assertion: The $6.61 cancellation fee was levied on the rider, but the fee only arises in the two published situations and Ryde's own rule for a 'rider cancels' case is that any cancellation within 3 minutes of matching is not chargeable; here the rider cancelled at 18:25:30, only 2 min 30 s after acceptance at 18:23:00, i.e. inside the free window.

There is no basis to treat the rider as a no-show (the only other route to the $6.61 fee): the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null) and the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so NS-1(i) and (ii) both fail.

GPS confirms the driver was never at the pickup point: his closest approach was 1806 m at 18:25:30 and he never came within 200 m, so the rider's statement that the driver was nowhere near is corroborated by the system record, not merely asserted.

The rider's cancellation was prompt and in good faith: she asked for an ETA at 18:23 and the driver only answered 'About 5 min, traffic' at 18:24, so at the moment she cancelled the driver was still several minutes and over 1.8 km away — no rule requires her to keep waiting, and the $6.61 deduction is unexplained by any published additional charge.

Because the fee fail-conditions are made out, the full $6.61 charged should be returned to the rider as a Ryde voucher; the amount equals the cancellation fee actually charged (F5) and the disputed fee is to be waived in full rather than cash-refunded.

Separately from the outcome of this case, the driver's record shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days against only 777 trips plus 2 disputes flagged, which warrants sending his account for Ryde review as an additional account action.

weaknesses: The rider cancelled unilaterally rather than waiting for the driver, so the other side will argue she deprived the driver of the trip; F2 shows she cancelled at 18:25:30 and the driver's statement (F9) says 'I was on my way when the rider cancelled.' The counter is that NS-4 makes the 3-minute rule mechanical, and F1 shows the driver was still 1806 m away.

The rider does not get a free cancellation merely because the driver was late or far: NS-4 expressly says the driver not having arrived is not a ground for a free rider cancellation, and there is no ETA-based waiver rule to rely on (no ETA field in the case file). The case therefore rests on the 3-minute window in F2, not on the driver's lateness.

Traffic was mildly slow on Boon Lay Way (F10, speed band 3, 20-29 km/h) and the driver cited traffic in chat (F8); the driver may use this to argue he was reasonably en route, though F11 records no incident and F10 is a single 20-29 km/h band that cannot justify the 1806 m gap in F1.

The rider's own message (F7) shows she was still awaiting the driver rather than fleeing a no-show, and a judge could read the 2 min 30 s cancellation as opportunistic; the answer is that NS-4 sets no motive test — any cancellation within 3:00 is free.
The requested remedy is a voucher, not cash (NS-7), so the client does not recover money in hand even if the claim succeeds.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled only 2 min 30 s after acceptance (18:23:00 → 18:25:30), which is inside the 3-minute window; under NS-4 a cancellation made within 3 minutes of matching is not chargeable, so the $6.61 fee fails for lack of a billing basis independent of any driver conduct.
The driver never entered the 200 m pickup radius — closest approach was 1806 m at 18:25:30 — so NS-1(i)(ii) can never be satisfied and this cannot be sustained as a rider no-show against the driver.
No 'I'm Here' tap is recorded (driver_pressed_here_at is null) and no arrival was recorded, so no waiting fee or no-show cancellation against the rider was ever asserted by the driver either.

The driver was actively en route and communicating; the recorded chat shows the rider asking for ETA at 18:23 and the driver replying 'About 5 min, traffic' at 18:24, consistent with the driver's statement that he was on his way when the rider cancelled.

Any delay was ordinary traffic, not driver fault: Boon Lay Way carried only a mid-band 20–29 km/h speed band with no incidents recorded and fair weather, so there is no basis to attribute the rider's cancellation to driver misconduct.

The rider's own profile (604 days, 4.9 rating, 0 disputes in 90 d) shows no pattern of abusive cancellation, while the driver's profile shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 d; the driver asks only that this case be resolved on the records, and accepts the $6.61 should be refunded rather than contested.

weaknesses: The driver's written statement 'I was on my way' (F9) is uncorroborated by any distance-progress record in the fact table, and his chat claim of 'About 5 min' (F8) is contradicted by the system record that he was still 1806 m away at 18:25:30 when the rider cancelled (F1/F2) — the rider will use F1 to argue the ETA given was misleading.

The driver's own profile shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 d (F14); the rider could argue this is a repeated pattern and push for flag_account, though profile facts alone cannot decide the case and NS-1 is not met here.

On the strict NS-4 read the rider gets the full $6.61 back; the driver's only arguable defence (that the ride was long enough to be worth waiting for) has no support in the facts, since the fee basis is the 3-minute rule, not the driver's conduct (F2, F5).

points.response: Agreed and adopted: the rider cancelled 2 min 30 s after acceptance (F2), inside the 3-minute free window, so NS-4 gives no billing basis for the $6.61 fee (F5).
Accepted: with the closest approach 1806 m and never inside 200 m (F1) and no recorded arrival (F3), NS-1 cannot be made out, which only strengthens the refund the rider seeks.
Accepted, and it disposes of the only other route to a $6.61 fee: with no 'I'm Here' tap (F4) and no arrival record (F3), neither NS-1 nor NS-6 can be satisfied, so the deduction stands unexplained.

The driver's goodwill in chat does not change the outcome: his 'About 5 min, traffic' at 18:24 (F8) is contradicted by the system record that he was still 1806 m away when the rider cancelled at 18:25:30 (F1, F2), and NS-3 confirms the rider bears no cancellation fee when the driver cancels or is at fault.

The rider does not need to prove driver misconduct — NS-4 makes the fee free regardless of cause — and in any case one mid-band reading on Boon Lay Way at 20–29 km/h with no incidents and fair weather (F10, F11, F12) cannot explain a 1806 m gap from the pickup point (F1).

We accept the driver's concession that the $6.61 should be refunded, and we maintain our additional account-review request: his profile shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F14), which under NS-3/RD-6-style account action warrants sending the account to Ryde even though profile facts cannot decide this case.

Conceded as to the arithmetic: F2 records acceptance at 18:23:00 and the rider's cancellation at 18:25:30, i.e. 2 min 30 s, which falls inside the 3:00 free window under NS-4, so the $6.61 (F5) has no basis and the driver does not contest its return.
Conceded: F3 shows driver_arrived_at is null and F4 shows driver_pressed_here_at is null, so neither NS-1(i) nor NS-1(ii) can be met and there is no route to a no-show fee against the rider.

Conceded: F1 records a closest approach of 1806 m at 18:25:30 and no entry inside 200 m, so the rider's account that the driver was nowhere near is corroborated by the system record rather than disproved.

The rider had no obligation to keep waiting, but the driver's position remains that he was genuinely en route and not at fault — F8 ('About 5 min, traffic') and F10 (Boon Lay Way at 20–29 km/h during 18:18–18:30, with no incident in F11 and fair weather in F12) explain the gap; this is mitigation of the driver's conduct, not a defence to the fee, which fails on F2 under NS-4 alone.

Conceded in substance; the driver asks that the $6.61 be returned as a Ryde voucher as NS-7 requires, and notes the amount is fixed by the cancellation fee on record at F5, with no cash component available under NS-7.

The driver opposes flag_account here: F14 is profile data only, it cannot decide this case, and NS-1 is not satisfied on F3/F4, so there is no repeated no-show violation in this case to escalate; the two prior upheld no-show disputes in F14 concern earlier tickets and this complaint rests solely on the 3-minute rule in F2.

The driver withdraws the framing in D6 insofar as it invites profile-based argument; the driver rests on F2 and NS-4 and does not ask the judge to weigh the rider's profile against the driver's record (F13, F14).
